projects.title: FK Education Platform
projects.summary: Coaching platform beside an open-source LMS: plans, reviews, lessons, parent view.
description: I built this for a coaching center that already had an open-source LMS but was running its weekly plans, lesson payments, and parent updates outside it. The platform adds what the core was never meant to own: weekly plans, evidence, coach reviews, mock exams, private lessons, billing, and a read-only parent view.
- 40 session-bound API endpoints and 10 custom tables beside an unmodified open-source LMS core
- Five roles with different visibility: student, coach, teacher, parent, admin
- Private lessons have their own pricing, payment, and audit trail
- 87 quality gates and a live smoke test run before each deploy
highlights: Built the custom domain layer beside the LMS core instead of forking it, so upstream security patches stay cheap
Authorization is four checks — session, role, capability, and target scope — plus field-level masking
Game access is tied to submitted evidence, not coach approval, which keeps the feedback loop short without losing the audit trail
The workflow that kept 40 endpoints and five roles consistent later became SpecOS
Planned and built with low-cost LLMs; the scaffolding that made it possible is now open source
projects.impact: Runs the daily coaching operations, lesson billing, and parent visibility for an education provider without forking its upstream LMS core

projects.title: SpecOS; architecture scaffolding for AI coding assistants
projects.summary: Architecture maps and rules that keep AI coding assistants from drifting.
description: SpecOS is the workflow I use to keep AI-assisted projects from drifting. You give it a plan or a PRD; it writes a small set of architecture maps and rules into the repo, and the assistant has to follow them instead of guessing.
- Sub-3KB map slices keep the assistant from re-reading a 50KB architecture document on every prompt
- A sibling-pairs matrix forces one-file changes to update the screens and endpoints that depend on them
- A strict DB → API → test → UI order blocks frontend work until the data layer is real
- A zero-dependency Node script verifies links, map sizes, and template leftovers before commit
highlights: Built after the same failure kept showing up on a real five-role education platform: one screen updated, two siblings forgotten
Cut the context needed to start a fresh session from tens of thousands of tokens to under 2,000
Open source, MIT, and deliberately extractable — generated rules keep working after the generator is removed
projects.impact: Turns a general-purpose coding assistant into a constrained builder that follows the project's architecture instead of inventing one

projects.title: debian tools
description: A toolkit that simplifies first setup through easy-to-use scripts for Debian-based systems.
- Quickly install popular software packages without remembering complex commands
- Automate routine system administration tasks
- Save time during system setup and maintenance
## Features
The toolkit offers scripts for:
- Browser installations (Brave, LibreWolf, Waterfox)
- VPN setups (Mullvad, ProtonVPN, IVPN)
- Development environments (Qt/QML/C++)
- System configurations (systemd-resolved, GRUB)
- Virtualization tools (QEMU/KVM, Waydroid)
- Android tools (Custom ROM installation, WiFi network backup)
highlights: Consolidated multi-step installations into single scripts
Implemented consistent error handling and user feedback
Added uninstallation options for all components
projects.impact: Reduced system setup time and eliminated repetitive googling for common tasks
